# Fundamental Group Element of a Loop on a Möbius Strip

## Setting Up the Möbius Strip

The standard embedding of a Möbius strip in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is:
$$M(u, v) = \bigl((1 + v\cos(u/2))\cos u,\; (1 + v\cos(u/2))\sin u,\; v\sin(u/2)\bigr)$$
where $u \in [0, 2\pi)$ and $v \in [-1, 1]$.

**The central (core) circle** corresponds to $v = 0$:
$$M(u, 0) = (\cos u,\; \sin u,\; 0)$$

This is the **unit circle in the $xy$-plane**, parameterized once as $u$ runs from $0$ to $2\pi$.

## Identifying the Loop

The given loop is:
$$\gamma(t) = (\cos 10\pi t,\; \sin 10\pi t), \quad t \in [0,1]$$

This is a unit circle in the $xy$-plane, so it lies entirely on the **core circle** of the Möbius strip (with $v=0$). To identify it with the parameter $u$:

$$u = 10\pi t$$

As $t$ goes from $0$ to $1$, the parameter $u$ sweeps from $0$ to $10\pi$.

## Counting Windings Around the Core

One full traversal of the core circle corresponds to $u$ advancing by $2\pi$. The number of complete loops is:

$$\frac{10\pi}{2\pi} = 5$$

## Computing the Fundamental Group Element

The Möbius strip **deformation retracts** onto its core circle $S^1$, so:
$$\pi_1(\text{Möbius strip}) \cong \pi_1(S^1) \cong \mathbb{Z}$$

The generator of $\mathbb{Z}$ is the loop that traverses the core circle **once**. Our loop traverses it **5 times**, so it represents the element $5$ in $\mathbb{Z}$.

$$\boxed{5}$$
